passages.text: Now Elisha had said to the woman whose son he had restored to life, “Arise, you and your household; go and live as a foreigner wherever you can. For the LORD has decreed a seven-year famine, and it has already come to the land.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha had restored the woman's son to life.
Elisha spoke to this woman.
He said, "Get up."
He said, "Go."
He said, "Take your household with you."
He said, "Live as a foreigner wherever you can."
He said, "The LORD has called for a famine."
He said, "The famine has come to the land."
He said, "The famine will last seven years."
passages.original: וֶאֱלִישָׁ֡ע דִּבֶּ֣ר אֶל־ הָאִשָּׁה֩ אֲשֶׁר־ הֶחֱיָ֨ה אֶת־ בְּנָ֜הּ לֵאמֹ֗ר ק֤וּמִי וּלְכִי֙ אַתִּי וּבֵיתֵ֔ךְ וְג֖וּרִי בַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר תָּג֑וּרִי כִּֽי־ קָרָ֤א יְהוָה֙ לָֽרָעָ֔ב וְגַם־ בָּ֥א אֶל־ הָאָ֖רֶץ שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: So the woman had proceeded to do as the man of God had instructed. And she and her household lived as foreigners for seven years in the land of the Philistines.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha had restored life to this woman's son.
Elisha told the woman to leave her home.
He told her to take her household with her.
He told her to live as a foreigner wherever she could.
The woman obeyed Elisha.
She took her household.
They went to the land of the Philistines.
They lived there as foreigners for seven years.
passages.original: וַתָּ֙קָם֙ הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וַתַּ֕עַשׂ כִּדְבַ֖ר אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וַתֵּ֤לֶךְ הִיא֙ וּבֵיתָ֔הּ וַתָּ֥גָר בְּאֶֽרֶץ־ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֖ים שֶׁ֥בַע שָׁנִֽים׃

passages.text: At the end of seven years, when the woman returned from the land of the Philistines, she went to the king to appeal for her house and her land.
passages.sermon:
A woman once lived in Israel.
Elisha, a prophet, had restored her son to life.
Elisha told her to leave her home because a famine would last seven years.
She obeyed Elisha.
She and her household lived in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
After seven years ended, the woman returned from the land of the Philistines.
She found her house and her land were no longer hers.
She went to the king.
She appealed to the king for her house and her land.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י מִקְצֵה֙ שֶׁ֣בַע שָׁנִ֔ים וַתָּ֥שָׁב הָאִשָּׁ֖ה מֵאֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֑ים וַתֵּצֵא֙ לִצְעֹ֣ק אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אֶל־ בֵּיתָ֖הּ וְאֶל־ שָׂדָֽהּ׃

passages.text: Now the king had been speaking to Gehazi, the servant of the man of God, saying, “Please relate to me all the great things Elisha has done.”
passages.sermon: The king spoke to Gehazi.\r\nGehazi was the servant of the man of God.\r\nThe king said to Gehazi, “Tell me all the great things Elisha has done.”
passages.original: וְהַמֶּ֗לֶךְ מְדַבֵּר֙ אֶל־ גֵּ֣חֲזִ֔י נַ֥עַר אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים לֵאמֹ֑ר סַפְּרָה־ נָּ֣א לִ֔י אֵ֥ת כָּל־ הַגְּדֹל֖וֹת אֲשֶׁר־ עָשָׂ֥ה אֱלִישָֽׁע׃

passages.text: And Gehazi was telling the king how Elisha had brought the dead back to life. Just then the woman whose son Elisha had revived came to appeal to the king for her house and her land. So Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman, and this is the son Elisha restored to life.”
passages.sermon:
Gehazi was speaking to the king.
Gehazi was the servant of Elisha, the man of God.
Gehazi told the king how Elisha brought a dead person back to life.
At that moment, a woman came to the king.
This woman’s son had been brought back to life by Elisha.
The woman cried out to the king for her house and her land.
Gehazi said, “My lord the king, this is the woman.”
Gehazi said, “This is her son, whom Elisha restored to life.”
passages.original: וַ֠יְהִי ה֥וּא מְסַפֵּ֣ר לַמֶּלֶךְ֮ אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ הֶחֱיָ֣ה אֶת־ הַמֵּת֒ וְהִנֵּ֨ה הָאִשָּׁ֜ה אֲשֶׁר־ הֶחֱיָ֤ה אֶת־ בְּנָהּ֙ צֹעֶ֣קֶת אֶל־ הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עַל־ בֵּיתָ֖הּ וְעַל־ שָׂדָ֑הּ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר גֵּֽחֲזִי֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ זֹ֚את הָֽאִשָּׁ֔ה וְזֶה־ בְּנָ֖הּ אֲשֶׁר־ הֶחֱיָ֥ה אֱלִישָֽׁע׃

passages.text: When the king asked the woman, she confirmed it. So the king appointed for her an officer, saying, “Restore all that was hers, along with all the proceeds of the field from the day that she left the country until now.”
passages.sermon:
The king spoke to the woman.
He asked her about her situation.
The woman answered the king.
She confirmed what had happened.
The king decided to help her.
He appointed an officer to assist her.
The king commanded the officer.
He said, “Return everything that belongs to her.”
He also said, “Give her all the produce from her field.”
He specified, “Give her the produce from the day she left the land until now.”
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁאַ֥ל הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ לָאִשָּׁ֖ה וַתְּסַפֶּר־ ל֑וֹ וַיִּתֶּן־ לָ֣הּ הַמֶּלֶךְ֩ סָרִ֨יס אֶחָ֜ד לֵאמֹ֗ר הָשֵׁ֤יב אֶת־ כָּל־ אֲשֶׁר־ לָהּ֙ וְאֵת֙ כָּל־ תְּבוּאֹ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה מִיּ֛וֹם עָזְבָ֥ה אֶת־ הָאָ֖רֶץ וְעַד־ עָֽתָּה׃פ

passages.text: Then Elisha came to Damascus while Ben-hadad king of Aram was sick, and the king was told, “The man of God has come here.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha came to the city of Damascus.
At that time, Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Ben-hadad was sick.
Someone told the king about Elisha.
They said, “The man of God has come here.”
passages.original: וַיָּבֹ֤א אֱלִישָׁע֙ דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וּבֶן־ הֲדַ֥ד מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֖ם חֹלֶ֑ה וַיֻּגַּד־ ל֣וֹ לֵאמֹ֔ר בָּ֛א אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים עַד־ הֵֽנָּה׃

passages.text: So the king said to Hazael, “Take a gift in your hand, go to meet the man of God, and inquire of the LORD through him, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’ ”
passages.sermon:
Ben-hadad was the king of Aram.
Ben-hadad was sick.
Ben-hadad spoke to Hazael.
Ben-hadad said, “Take a gift in your hand.”
He said, “Go to meet the man of God.”
He said, “Ask the LORD through him.”
He said, “Ask if I will recover from this illness.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ אֶל־ חֲזָהאֵ֗ל קַ֤ח בְּיָֽדְךָ֙ מִנְחָ֔ה וְלֵ֕ךְ לִקְרַ֖את אִ֣ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְדָרַשְׁתָּ֨ אֶת־ יְהוָ֤ה מֵֽאוֹתוֹ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֶחְיֶ֖ה מֵחֳלִ֥י זֶֽה׃

passages.text: So Hazael went to meet Elisha, taking with him a gift of forty camel loads of every good thing from Damascus. And he went in and stood before him and said, “Your son Ben-hadad king of Aram has sent me to ask, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’ ”
passages.sermon:
Hazael was a servant of Ben-hadad, king of Aram.
Ben-hadad was sick.
Ben-hadad sent Hazael to Elisha, the man of God.
Hazael took a gift with him.
The gift was every good thing from Damascus.
The gift filled forty camels.
Hazael went to Elisha.
Hazael stood before Elisha.
Hazael spoke to Elisha.
Hazael said, “Your son Ben-hadad, king of Aram, sent me to you.”
Hazael said, “He asks, ‘Will I recover from this illness?’”
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ חֲזָאֵל֮ לִקְרָאתוֹ֒ וַיִּקַּ֨ח מִנְחָ֤ה בְיָדוֹ֙ וְכָל־ ט֣וּב דַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק מַשָּׂ֖א אַרְבָּעִ֣ים גָּמָ֑ל וַיָּבֹא֙ וַיַּעֲמֹ֣ד לְפָנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֗אמֶר בִּנְךָ֨ בֶן־ הֲדַ֤ד מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָם֙ שְׁלָחַ֤נִי אֵלֶ֙יךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הַאֶחְיֶ֖ה מֵחֳלִ֥י זֶֽה׃

passages.text: Elisha answered, “Go and tell him, ‘You will surely recover.’ But the LORD has shown me that in fact he will die.”
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet of the LORD.
Elisha spoke to Hazael.
Elisha said, "Go and tell Ben-hadad, 'You will surely recover.'"
But Elisha also said, "The LORD has shown me that Ben-hadad will die."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אֱלִישָׁ֔ע לֵ֥ךְ אֱמָר־ לֹא חָיֹ֣ה תִחְיֶ֑ה וְהִרְאַ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה כִּֽי־ מ֥וֹת יָמֽוּת׃

passages.text: Elisha fixed his gaze steadily on him until Hazael became uncomfortable. Then the man of God began to weep.
passages.sermon:
Elisha was a prophet and a man of God.
Elisha looked directly at Hazael.
Elisha stared at Hazael for a long time.
Hazael became uncomfortable.
Then Elisha, the man of God, began to weep.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲמֵ֥ד אֶת־ פָּנָ֖יו וַיָּ֣שֶׂם עַד־ בֹּ֑שׁ וַיֵּ֖בְךְּ אִ֥ישׁ הָאֱלֹהִֽים׃

passages.text: “Why is my lord weeping?” asked Hazael. “Because I know the evil you will do to the Israelites,” Elisha replied. “You will set fire to their fortresses, kill their young men with the sword, dash their little ones to pieces, and rip open their pregnant women.”
passages.sermon:
Hazael spoke to Elisha.
Hazael asked, “Why is my lord weeping?”
Elisha was a prophet of God.
Elisha answered Hazael.
Elisha said, “I know what you will do to the people of Israel.”
Elisha said, “You will do evil to them.”
Elisha said, “You will burn their strongholds with fire.”
Elisha said, “You will kill their young men with the sword.”
Elisha said, “You will dash their little children to pieces.”
Elisha said, “You will rip open their pregnant women.”
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חֲזָאֵ֔ל מַדּ֖וּעַ אֲדֹנִ֣י בֹכֶ֑ה וַיֹּ֡אמֶר כִּֽי־ יָדַ֡עְתִּי אֵ֣ת אֲשֶׁר־ תַּעֲשֶׂה֩ לִבְנֵ֨י יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל רָעָ֗ה מִבְצְרֵיהֶ֞ם תְּשַׁלַּ֤ח בָּאֵשׁ֙ וּבַחֻֽרֵיהֶם֙ בַּחֶ֣רֶב תַּהֲרֹ֔ג וְעֹלְלֵיהֶ֣ם תְּרַטֵּ֔שׁ וְהָרֹתֵיהֶ֖ם תְּבַקֵּֽעַ׃

passages.text: “But how could your servant, a mere dog, do such a monstrous thing?” said Hazael. And Elisha answered, “The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram.”
passages.sermon:
Hazael spoke to Elisha.
Hazael said, "I am your servant."
Hazael called himself a dog.
Hazael asked, "How could I do such a great and terrible thing?"
Elisha answered Hazael.
Elisha said, "The LORD has shown me something."
Elisha said, "You will be king over Aram."
passages.original: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חֲזָהאֵ֔ל כִּ֣י מָ֤ה עַבְדְּךָ֙ הַכֶּ֔לֶב כִּ֣י יַעֲשֶׂ֔ה הַדָּבָ֥ר הַגָּד֖וֹל הַזֶּ֑ה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֱלִישָׁ֔ע הִרְאַ֧נִי יְהוָ֛ה אֹתְךָ֖ מֶ֥לֶךְ עַל־ אֲרָֽם׃

passages.text: So Hazael left Elisha and went to his master, who asked him, “What did Elisha say to you?” And he replied, “He told me that you would surely recover.”
passages.sermon:
Hazael left Elisha.
Hazael went to his master.
His master was the king of Aram.
The king asked Hazael, “What did Elisha say to you?”
Hazael answered the king.
Hazael said, “He told me that you would surely recover.”
passages.original: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ׀ מֵאֵ֣ת אֱלִישָׁ֗ע וַיָּבֹא֙ אֶל־ אֲדֹנָ֔יו וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ מָֽה־ אָמַ֥ר לְךָ֖ אֱלִישָׁ֑ע וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָ֥מַר לִ֖י חָיֹ֥ה תִחְיֶֽה׃

passages.text: But the next day Hazael took a thick cloth, dipped it in water, and spread it over the king’s face. So Ben-hadad died, and Hazael reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Hazael was a servant of the king of Aram, Ben-hadad.
The next day, Hazael took a thick cloth.
He dipped the cloth in water.
He spread the wet cloth over Ben-hadad’s face.
Ben-hadad died.
Hazael became king of Aram after him.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י מִֽמָּחֳרָ֗ת וַיִּקַּ֤ח הַמַּכְבֵּר֙ וַיִּטְבֹּ֣ל בַּמַּ֔יִם וַיִּפְרֹ֥שׂ עַל־ פָּנָ֖יו וַיָּמֹ֑ת וַיִּמְלֹ֥ךְ חֲזָהאֵ֖ל תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

passages.text: In the fifth year of the reign of Joram son of Ahab over Israel, Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat succeeded his father as king of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Joram was the son of Ahab.
Joram was king of Israel.
Jehoshaphat was king of Judah.
In the fifth year of Joram’s reign over Israel, Jehoram became king of Judah.
Jehoram was the son of Jehoshaphat.
Jehoram succeeded his father as king of Judah.
passages.original: וּבִשְׁנַ֣ת חָמֵ֗שׁ לְיוֹרָ֤ם בֶּן־ אַחְאָב֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וִיהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֑ה מָלַ֛ךְ יְהוֹרָ֥ם בֶּן־ יְהוֹשָׁפָ֖ט מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem eight years.
passages.sermon:
Jehoram became king of Judah.
Jehoram was thirty-two years old when he became king.
Jehoram ruled in Jerusalem.
Jehoram reigned for eight years.
passages.original: בֶּן־ שְׁלֹשִׁ֥ים וּשְׁתַּ֛יִם שָׁנָ֖ה הָיָ֣ה בְמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׁמֹנֶ֣ה שָׁנָה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָֽם׃

passages.text: And Jehoram walked in the ways of the kings of Israel, just as the house of Ahab had done. For he married a daughter of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Jehoram was king of Judah.
Jehoram followed the ways of the kings of Israel.
The house of Ahab had acted in these same ways.
Jehoram married a daughter of Ahab.
Jehoram did evil in the sight of the LORD.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ׀ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר עָשׂוּ֙ בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֔ב כִּ֚י בַּת־ אַחְאָ֔ב הָֽיְתָה־ לּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיַּ֥עַשׂ הָרַ֖ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָֽה׃

passages.text: Yet for the sake of His servant David, the LORD was unwilling to destroy Judah, since He had promised to maintain a lamp for David and his descendants forever.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD did not want to destroy Judah.
The LORD remembered David.
David was the LORD’s servant.
The LORD had made a promise to David.
The LORD promised to give David a lamp.
The LORD promised this lamp to David’s children.
The LORD promised to keep this lamp for all time.
passages.original: וְלֹֽא־ אָבָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לְהַשְׁחִ֣ית אֶת־ יְהוּדָ֔ה לְמַ֖עַן דָּוִ֣ד עַבְדּ֑וֹ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אָֽמַר־ ל֗וֹ לָתֵ֨ת ל֥וֹ נִ֛יר לְבָנָ֖יו כָּל־ הַיָּמִֽים׃

passages.text: In the days of Jehoram, Edom rebelled against the hand of Judah and appointed their own king.
passages.sermon: Jehoram was king of Judah.\r\nDuring Jehoram’s reign, Edom rebelled against Judah.\r\nEdom chose their own king.
passages.original: בְּיָמָיו֙ פָּשַׁ֣ע אֱד֔וֹם מִתַּ֖חַת יַד־ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיַּמְלִ֥כוּ עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם מֶֽלֶךְ׃

passages.text: So Jehoram crossed over to Zair with all his chariots. When the Edomites surrounded him and his chariot commanders, he rose up and attacked by night. His troops, however, fled to their homes.
passages.sermon:
Jehoram was king of Judah.
Jehoram took all his chariots with him.
Jehoram crossed over to Zair.
The Edomites surrounded Jehoram.
The Edomites also surrounded his chariot commanders.
Jehoram got up at night.
Jehoram attacked the Edomites at night.
Jehoram struck the Edomites who surrounded him.
Jehoram also struck the chariot commanders of the Edomites.
Jehoram’s troops ran away.
Jehoram’s troops fled to their homes.
passages.original: וַיַּעֲבֹ֤ר יוֹרָם֙ צָעִ֔ירָה וְכָל־ הָרֶ֖כֶב עִמּ֑וֹ וַֽיְהִי־ ה֞וּא קָ֣ם לַ֗יְלָה וַיַּכֶּ֨ה אֶת־ אֱד֜וֹם הַסֹּבֵ֤יב אֵלָיו֙ וְאֵת֙ שָׂרֵ֣י הָרֶ֔כֶב וַיָּ֥נָס הָעָ֖ם לְאֹהָלָֽיו׃

passages.text: So to this day Edom has been in rebellion against the hand of Judah. Likewise, Libnah rebelled at the same time.
passages.sermon: Edom rebelled against the rule of Judah.\r\nEdom has remained in rebellion until today.\r\nAt that same time, Libnah also rebelled.
passages.original: וַיִּפְשַׁ֣ע אֱד֗וֹם מִתַּ֙חַת֙ יַד־ יְהוּדָ֔ה עַ֖ד הַיּ֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה אָ֛ז תִּפְשַׁ֥ע לִבְנָ֖ה בָּעֵ֥ת הַהִֽיא׃

passages.text: As for the rest of the acts of Jehoram, along with all his accomplishments, are they not written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?
passages.sermon:
Jehoram was king of Judah.
He did many things during his reign.
Other acts of Jehoram are not listed here.
All his accomplishments are recorded elsewhere.
They are written in the book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah.
passages.original: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י יוֹרָ֖ם וְכָל־ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֽוֹא־ הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל־ סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: And Jehoram rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David. And his son Ahaziah reigned in his place.
passages.sermon:
Jehoram was king of Judah.
Jehoram died.
Jehoram joined his ancestors in death.
People buried Jehoram with his ancestors.
They buried him in the City of David.
Ahaziah was Jehoram’s son.
Ahaziah became king after Jehoram.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב יוֹרָם֙ עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר עִם־ אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו׃פ

passages.text: In the twelfth year of the reign of Joram son of Ahab over Israel, Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah.
passages.sermon:
Joram was the son of Ahab.
Joram was king of Israel.
Joram ruled Israel for twelve years.
Ahaziah was the son of Jehoram.
Jehoram was king of Judah.
In the twelfth year of Joram’s reign over Israel, Ahaziah became king of Judah.
passages.original: בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁתֵּים־ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְיוֹרָ֥ם בֶּן־ אַחְאָ֖ב מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל מָלַ֛ךְ אֲחַזְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־ יְהוֹרָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה׃

passages.text: Ahaziah was twenty-two years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem one year. His mother’s name was Athaliah, the granddaughter of Omri king of Israel.
passages.sermon:
Ahaziah became king when he was twenty-two years old.
He ruled in Jerusalem.
He ruled for one year.
His mother was Athaliah.
Athaliah was the granddaughter of Omri.
Omri was king of Israel.
passages.original: בֶּן־ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וּשְׁתַּ֤יִם שָׁנָה֙ אֲחַזְיָ֣הוּ בְמָלְכ֔וֹ וְשָׁנָ֣ה אַחַ֔ת מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְשֵׁ֤ם אִמּוֹ֙ עֲתַלְיָ֔הוּ בַּת־ עָמְרִ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

passages.text: And Ahaziah walked in the ways of the house of Ahab and did evil in the sight of the LORD like the house of Ahab, for he was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
passages.sermon:
Ahaziah was king of Judah.
Ahaziah followed the example of the house of Ahab.
Ahaziah did evil in the sight of the LORD.
Ahaziah acted like the house of Ahab.
Ahaziah was a son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֗לֶךְ בְּדֶ֙רֶךְ֙ בֵּ֣ית אַחְאָ֔ב וַיַּ֧עַשׂ הָרַ֛ע בְּעֵינֵ֥י יְהוָ֖ה כְּבֵ֣ית אַחְאָ֑ב כִּ֛י חֲתַ֥ן בֵּית־ אַחְאָ֖ב הֽוּא׃

passages.text: Then Ahaziah went with Joram son of Ahab to fight against Hazael king of Aram at Ramoth-gilead, and the Arameans wounded Joram.
passages.sermon:
Ahaziah was king of Judah.
Joram was the son of Ahab.
Joram was king of Israel.
Hazael was king of Aram.
Ahaziah went with Joram.
They went to fight Hazael.
They fought at Ramoth-gilead.
The Arameans fought against them.
The Arameans wounded Joram.
passages.original: וַיֵּ֜לֶךְ אֶת־ יוֹרָ֣ם בֶּן־ אַחְאָ֗ב לַמִּלְחָמָ֛ה עִם־ חֲזָהאֵ֥ל מֶֽלֶךְ־ אֲרָ֖ם בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד וַיַּכּ֥וּ אֲרַמִּ֖ים אֶת־ יוֹרָֽם׃

passages.text: So King Joram returned to Jezreel to recover from the wounds that the Arameans had inflicted on him at Ramah when he fought against Hazael king of Aram. Then Ahaziah son of Jehoram king of Judah went down to Jezreel to visit Joram son of Ahab, because Joram had been wounded.
passages.sermon:
King Joram was the king of Israel.
The Arameans wounded King Joram at Ramah.
King Joram fought against Hazael, king of Aram, at Ramah.
King Joram returned to Jezreel.
He went there to recover from his wounds.
Ahaziah was the son of Jehoram.
Ahaziah was the king of Judah.
Ahaziah went down to Jezreel.
He went to visit Joram, the son of Ahab.
Joram was in Jezreel because he was wounded.
passages.original: וַיָּשָׁב֩ יוֹרָ֨ם הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לְהִתְרַפֵּ֣א בְיִזְרְעֶ֗אל מִן־ הַמַּכִּים֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַכֻּ֤הוּ אֲרַמִּים֙ בָּֽרָמָ֔ה בְּהִלָּ֣חֲמ֔וֹ אֶת־ חֲזָהאֵ֖ל מֶ֣לֶךְ אֲרָ֑ם וַאֲחַזְיָ֨הוּ בֶן־ יְהוֹרָ֜ם מֶ֣לֶךְ יְהוּדָ֗ה יָרַ֡ד לִרְא֞וֹת אֶת־ יוֹרָ֧ם בֶּן־ אַחְאָ֛ב בְּיִזְרְעֶ֖אל כִּֽי־ חֹלֶ֥ה הֽוּא׃פ
